# Toronto Lease Renewal: Rent Increase Check

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You have a clear renewal moment: lease end on **2026-08-31** and a proposed **9% increase** starting **2026-09-01**. The safest approach is to confirm the notice details, ask for the legal basis and calculation, and keep everything in writing.

## Tenant Rights Questions and Document Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

| Topic | Questions to Ask | What to Gather |
|---|---|---|
| Notice details | Was the increase given in writing? Does it state the current rent, new rent, and effective date? | Lease, renewal notice, email/text history |
| Legal basis | Is the unit subject to any rent-control rules or exemptions? What rule supports the 9% amount? | Property address, lease start date, prior notices |
| Timing | Was enough notice provided before 2026-09-01? | Copy of notice with date received |
| Calculation | How was 9% calculated from the current rent? Can you show the math? | Current rent statement, proposed amount |
| Negotiation | Is the landlord open to a smaller increase, phased increase, or longer renewal term? | Your payment history, comparable listings if you choose to use them |
| Repairs and condition | Are there unresolved repair issues that affect value or habitability? | Photos, repair requests, inspection notes |
| Payment method | Will anything else change besides rent, such as utilities, parking, or deposits? | Current lease addenda, receipts |
| Next steps | What deadline do you want for my response? Can we confirm the terms by email? | A written record of all replies |

### What to gather before replying
- Current lease and any renewal draft
- Rent payment records for the full tenancy
- All landlord emails/texts about the increase
- Any repair requests, maintenance tickets, or inspection photos
- A clean copy of the proposed new rent amount and effective date
- A short list of comparable rents, if you want to support a negotiation
- Your preferred fallback options: smaller increase, fixed term, month-to-month, or longer renewal

## Practical Negotiation Points

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-square-text.svg

- Ask for the **exact reason** for the increase and whether it is negotiable.
- Request a **written breakdown** of how the new rent was set.
- Offer a **counterproposal** that is easier for you to accept, such as a lower increase or a longer lease term.
- If the unit has ongoing issues, ask whether a **repair timeline** or rent adjustment is possible.
- Keep the tone calm and factual; avoid agreeing verbally before you review the details.
- Save every reply so you have a complete paper trail.

## Polite Email Draft Requesting Clarification and Negotiation

Subject: Lease Renewal and Rent Increase Clarification

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

Thank you for sending the renewal notice for my apartment. I am reviewing the proposed rent increase of 9% effective 2026-09-01.

Before I respond, could you please confirm the following:
- the current rent amount used in the calculation
- the legal or contractual basis for the increase
- how the 9% figure was calculated
- whether any other lease terms are changing

I have been a responsible tenant and have appreciated living here. Based on my budget, I would like to ask whether there is any flexibility on the proposed increase. If possible, I would be interested in discussing a smaller increase or another arrangement that could work for both of us.

Please let me know when you are available, or feel free to reply by email with the details. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best regards,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone Number]
